contradiction_resolution: No claim-level contradiction: contradicts_claim_ids is empty, and the statement does not oppose CONJ-0001, THM-0001-THM-0007, OBS-0001, or RED-0001, all of which are Q-Hodge-theoretic statements about M_{g,n} / Mbar_{g,n}, whereas FND-0131 is a coherent-sheaf base-change statement about the CE evaluation complex. VERDICT: promote candidate -> corroborated; evidence_class upgraded adversarial_review -> primary_source; merge_target none. (1) PRIMARY-SOURCE VERIFICATION OF WHAT HOLDS UNCONDITIONALLY. Stacks Project Lemma 36.30.4 (tag 0B91, retrieved from section page tag 0A1G): for f proper of finite presentation and G finitely presented and flat over S, Rf_*G is a perfect object of D(O_S) and its formation commutes with arbitrary base change; Remark 36.30.2 (tag 0A1I) gives the classical Mumford form, a finite complex M^. of finite projective R-modules with RGamma(X_{R'},G_{R'}) = M^. ox_R R' functorially. Lemma 36.32.1 (tag 0BDN) gives semicontinuity of beta_i(s) = dim_{k(s)} H^i(X_s,F_s) and its compatibility with base change; Lemma 36.32.2 (tag 0B9T) gives local constancy of chi. So the two-term-complex model presupposed by the finding is correct and the fibre dimensions are computed by K ox^L k(s) over any base. (2) PRIMARY-SOURCE VERIFICATION THAT THE INFERENCE THE FINDING DENIES IS EXACTLY THE ONE THAT NEEDS REDUCEDNESS. Algebra Lemma 10.78.3 (tag 0FWG) states the equivalence 'M finite with rho_M(p) = dim_{k(p)} M ox k(p) locally constant <=> M finite projective' UNDER THE HYPOTHESIS 'Let R be a reduced ring'; the page records that reducedness is what licenses the appeal to Lemma 10.25.2 (checking injectivity at minimal primes). Schemes/Modules Lemma 28.21.3 (section tag 05P1) is the scheme-level restatement, again with the reduced hypothesis. The Stacks Project deliberately has no unrestricted 'constant fibre dimension => locally free' statement; instead Lemma 36.32.3 (tag 0B9S) formulates the correct universal version as an OPEN SUBSCHEME U ⊂ S such that T -> S factors through U iff Rf_{T,*}F_T is finite locally free of rank r in degree i. That is precisely the 'separate scheme-theoretic constant-rank argument' FND-0131 demands, and its existence as a scheme-theoretic (not set-theoretic) condition is the content of the finding. (3) INDEPENDENT MECHANISM, MADE EXACT. Write K = [E^0 --phi--> E^1] with E^1 of rank m. Constancy of h^0 is equivalent to constancy of rank(phi_s) = rk E^0 - h^0(s) =: r at every point. The two halves of 'rank = r' behave asymmetrically. Lower bound: rank(phi_s) >= r at every point <=> V(I_r(phi)) = empty <=> I_r(phi) = O_B, a genuine scheme-theoretic conclusion insensitive to nilpotents. Upper bound: rank(phi_s) <= r at every point only gives that every (r+1)-minor lies in every prime, i.e. I_{r+1}(phi) ⊆ nil(O_B), NOT I_{r+1}(phi) = 0. Since coker(phi) has presentation matrix phi, Fit_j(coker phi) = I_{m-j}(phi), and by More on Algebra Lemma 15.8.8 (tag 07ZD, retrieved via section tag 07Z6) coker(phi) is finite locally free of rank c = m - r iff Fit_{c-1} = 0 and Fit_c = O_B, i.e. iff I_{r+1}(phi) = 0 and I_r(phi) = O_B. On a reduced base nil = 0 and the pointwise upper bound upgrades to the ideal-theoretic one - which is exactly why Grauert carries reducedness, and exactly what fails otherwise. Once coker(phi) = H^1(K) is locally free the sequence splits locally and ker(phi) = H^0(K) is locally free too, so the two clauses stand or fall together. (4) EXPLICIT COUNTEREXAMPLE (verified by me, not taken from a source). B = Spec k[e]/(e^2), K = [O_B --e--> O_B]. B has a single point, so all fibre dimensions are trivially constant: h^0 = h^1 = 1. But H^0(K) = ker = (e) ≅ k and H^1(K) = coker = k are not free over k[e]/(e^2), and Fit_0(coker) = (e) is a nonzero nilpotent ideal, confirming the mechanism of (3). Base change also genuinely fails: the map H^0(K) ox k(s) -> H^0(K ox k(s)) sends e ox 1 to the class of e in R/eR = 0, hence is the ZERO map between two one-dimensional k-vector spaces. So a single example witnesses both clauses of the finding ('locally free cohomology' and 'arbitrary base change'). (5) THE PATHOLOGY IS GEOMETRICALLY REALIZED BY p_*L ON A CURVE FAMILY, NOT MERELY FORMAL. Let C/k be smooth projective of genus g, L_0 in Pic^{g-1}(C) with h^0(L_0) = h^1(L_0) = 1, and let L on C x_k Spec k[e]/(e^2) be the deformation of L_0 with Kodaira-Spencer class xi in H^1(C,O_C). The sequence 0 -> L_0 -> L -> L_0 -> 0 gives connecting map cup-xi: H^0(L_0) -> H^1(L_0), which is Serre-dual to multiplication by a nonzero section H^0(omega ox L_0^{-1}) -> H^0(omega) (injective on integral C), hence surjective, hence nonzero for suitable xi. For such xi one gets p_*L ≅ k and R^1p_*L ≅ k, neither locally free over k[e]/(e^2), with h^0 ≡ h^1 ≡ 1 on fibres and the base-change map zero. This is exactly the shape of object C66-COMP-RANK manipulates (pushforward of a relative line bundle on a family of curves), and the degeneration sits over an Abel-Jacobi/theta locus - i.e. over precisely the loci whose infinitesimal (nonreduced) neighbourhoods the campaign's determinantal scheme structures live on (cf. FND-0046, FND-0087, FND-0107). (6) SCOPE SHARPENINGS, none defeating: (P1)-(P4) in the scope block. The only substantive precision is (P1): 'arbitrary base change' in the finding's first sentence must be read as base change for the individual sheaves H^0(K), H^1(K), since the derived statement is unconditionally true by tag 0B91; without that reading the finding would over-reach. (P3) is a free strengthening (one degree suffices, by local constancy of chi). (P4) confirms the remedy clause is precise and satisfiable rather than open-ended. These are refinements of phrasing, not corrections of substance, so promotion is not blocked. (7) DUPLICATE / MERGE ANALYSIS against every adjudicated finding in packet C66-001-v4. FND-0122 is the COMPLEMENT, not a duplicate: it concludes I_11(phi) = I_5(phi_5) = O_B on any locally Noetherian base from geometric-fibre rank ranges {11,12} and {5,6}; by (3) that is exactly the pointwise LOWER-bound direction, which is legitimate and unaffected. FND-0131 blocks the converse direction (I_{r+1}(phi) = 0) that would be needed to call the cohomology sheaves bundles. The two should be read together as a matched pair; neither subsumes the other. FND-0047 concerns the case where h^0(L) JUMPS (relative linear system vs Proj pi_*L); FND-0131 concerns the case where h^0 is CONSTANT and still fails - complementary, distinct. FND-0107 says Proj(pi_*L) 'has correct fibres only over the open where h^0(L) is constant'; FND-0131 sharpens this: over a nonreduced base the set-theoretic constancy locus can be all of B while the conclusion still fails, and the correct universal formulation is the open subscheme of tag 0B9S. Record as a cross-reference/sharpening, not a contradiction (FND-0107's phrasing is standard and implicitly reduced/flat). FND-0099 invokes 'commutation of the cokernel with base change and Nakayama to descend from geometric fibres to the sheaf' and discharges it by degree vanishings (deg W_4 = 20 > 2g-2 = 10); that is an instance of remedy (ii) (tag 0D4E), so FND-0099 is an application of the correct discipline rather than a duplicate of the general caution. FND-0087 also concerns nonreduced bases but is about compatible reduction of the ordered-to-unordered torsor and flatness - different object, different failure mode. FND-0046 is the closest sibling in motif (fibrewise equivalence establishes equality only on geometric points; determinantal/Fitting scheme structures must be compared) but concerns identification of two LOCI, whereas FND-0131 concerns local freeness and base change of PUSHFORWARD SHEAVES, with a different remedy; keep separate and cross-reference. No other adjudicated finding (FND-0001, 0005, 0020, 0022, 0031-0037, 0048-0075, 0083-0086, 0089-0105, 0120, 0121, 0125, 0129, 0130) touches coherent base change. Merge target: none. scope.exact_assertion_upheld: Local constancy of s |-> dim_{k(s)} H^i(K ox^L k(s)) over a possibly nonreduced B does NOT imply that the individual cohomology sheaves H^0(K), H^1(K) are finite locally free, nor that their formation commutes with base change. The classical inference (Grauert) is licensed only after a reducedness hypothesis or an equivalent scheme-theoretic input.
excluded: the derived/perfect-complex base change statement, which holds over arbitrary bases
any claim about Q-coefficient weight or Tate structure; FND-0131 is a coherent-sheaf statement and carries no Hodge-theoretic content
scope.generality: Holds for any two-term complex K = [E^0 --phi--> E^1] of finite locally free modules (equivalently any perfect complex of tor-amplitude in [0,1]) on any locally Noetherian base scheme or algebraic stack B; in particular for K representing Rp_*L with p: C -> B a proper flat family of curves and L a B-flat line bundle. Nothing in the statement is specific to (g,n)=(6,6); the (6,6) instance is the CE evaluation map phi and its filtered quotient phi_5 of FND-0122.
objects: Fitting ideals Fit_j(coker phi) = I_{rk E^1 - j}(phi)
required_precisions: (P1) The denial is about the individual cohomology sheaves only. The DERIVED statement is unconditional: Rp_*L is a perfect object whose formation commutes with arbitrary base change (Stacks 36.30.4 / tag 0B91; Mumford's finite complex of finite projectives, Remark 36.30.2 / tag 0A1I). An attempt must not cite FND-0131 to cast doubt on K ox^L k(s) computing fibre cohomology, on semicontinuity (36.32.1 / 0BDN), or on local constancy of chi (36.32.2 / 0B9T).

(P2) 'geometric fibres' versus 'all scheme points' is not the operative distinction: dim_{k(s)} H^i(K ox k(s)) is invariant under residue-field extension, so constancy on geometric fibres is equivalent to constancy at all points of B. Reducedness, not the choice of test points, is what is missing.
(P3) Because chi = h^0 - h^1 is locally constant, constancy of h^0 and constancy of h^1 are equivalent hypotheses; the finding's 'constant dimensions' need only be assumed in one degree.

(P4) The obstruction is vacuous on reduced bases, and is dischargeable without reducedness by any of the named 'separate arguments': (i) the Fitting/minor-ideal condition I_{r+1}(phi) = 0 together with I_r(phi) = O_B (More on Algebra 15.8.8 / tag 07ZD, via Fit_j(coker phi) = I_{rk E^1 - j}(phi)); (ii) one-sided vanishing R^i = 0 for i > 0 (36.32.4 / tag 0D4E), which is the route already used by FND-0099; (iii) factoring B through the open subscheme U ⊂ B of 36.32.3 / tag 0B9S that universally represents 'Rp_* is finite locally free of rank r in degree i'. So the finding's remedy clause is accurate and satisfiable, not an unbounded demand.
